finding: [&>*]:h-auto/min-h-8 applied to EVERY child distorts non-default Button sizes (lg 36px->32px; icon-sm/xs no longer square) and leaks padding/min-height onto plain layout children.

Doc claimed the child rules win by SPECIFICITY; both are (0,1,0) and the override actually wins by Tailwind emission order. Reader would draw a wrong conclusion about !important/inline-style children.

Nested nav group received flex-wrap but NOT max-w-full/whitespace-normal: CardActions' rules reach direct children only, so a single over-wide nav label reproduces the original unreachable-overflow defect inside the fix.
justify-between + wrap degenerates: a wrapped line holding ONE item is placed at main-START, so the nav group jumps to the inline-start edge once the row wraps.
min-w-0 on a `truncate` element is a no-op (overflow:hidden already yields automatic-min-size 0) and the comment attributed causal weight to it.
measureReach treated overflow:hidden WITH overflow as user-scrollable, so the END-edge mirror of the defect under test would have measured green. overflow:hidden is not user-scrollable.
TEST-4 asserted DOM order via ascending raw `left`, encoding LTR as an invariant in a repo that mandates direction-agnostic UI.

After wrapping, 'Approve for this conversation' renders as a full-width, filled, ~2-line button while Deny stays 81x32 outline: relative prominence on the consent surface now favours the broadest approval. No test guards relative prominence.
TEST-8 accepted a tool name CSS-truncated to 60px; the name is attacker-controlled, and a truncated name is misleading rather than merely less legible.
flex-wrap lets an unbounded, nowrap, attacker-supplied server label take a whole line and displace the authentic '— needs approval' status onto another.
Target-size asymmetry favours the risky action: Deny stays 81x32 (below the taxonomy G5 44px mobile floor) while the broadest approval becomes ~238x48.
whitespace-normal without text-center gives a wrapped 2-line label ragged inline-start lines inside a flex-centred button.
CardActionsProps does not require data-testid, diverging from CardProps/ButtonProps; tests must select on a raw [data-slot] attribute outside the testid registry.
TEST-5 was paper coverage: the elicitation footer (~146px of a ~238px row) never overflowed at 390px, so every reachability assertion passed identically on the pre-fix markup.
TEST-3/TEST-4 compared viewport-relative `top` values sampled across separate scrollIntoViewIfNeeded calls; scroll drift could make an unwrapped row look wrapped (and vice versa).
gotoUntilVisible retried on ANY error, so a genuinely intermittent product regression was indistinguishable from the environmental import failure it documented.
Retry budget (3x12s + 25s) exceeded the 60s per-test timeout, so the carefully saved error could never actually be rethrown.
TEST-4's reading-order assertion is tautological when the selector matches 0 or 1 elements; nothing asserted the control count.
TEST-7 sums POST-FIX rendered widths (which the fix itself shrinks by wrapping labels), so it constrains the implementation rather than the property.
measureReach ignores containing-block semantics for absolutely-positioned descendants and clip-path/border-radius.
Every test drove the VIEWPORT, so the primitive's motivating case — a narrow CONTAINER at a wide viewport, the reason the rule is content-driven — was untested.
TEST-6 asserted only getComputedStyle(nested).flexWrap === 'wrap' — a restatement of the class just written, and provably insufficient for a single over-wide item.
The agent-facing manifest documented the new primitive as '_No always-required props._', conveying none of its opinionated child normalization.
The documented escape hatch ('set the height on the row via className') does not work — a row-level height cannot reach the [&>*] rules.
Nothing makes the broken hand-rolled pattern hard to reach; no lint flags `footer={<div className="...justify-end...">}`.
CardActions wraps in DOM order while the sibling DialogFooter/AlertDialogFooter stack in REVERSE (primary on top); the order divergence between three sibling action-row primitives was undocumented.
CardActionsProps omits the KitStyleProps intersection every sibling kit primitive carries, and the comment mis-described it as 'style-gated, like CardProps'.
The header's secondary labels keep whitespace-nowrap with no truncate of their own, so at ~320px a single very long server label can still protrude.
[&>*]:py-1 applied to a plain wrapper div grows the wizard footer ~8px at EVERY width, contradicting the primitive's 'inert when it fits' contract.
The [&>*] block encodes 'every child is a 32px default Button' with no opt-out, so a footer holding a Select/Checkbox/Text or an lg action cannot adopt the primitive without editing it.

The '101 call sites' figure that justified an opt-in primitive over fixing CardFooter counts Drawer/Modal footers too; only ~37 are Card footers, ~7 hand-rolled. The remaining Card footers keep the latent trap.
Same starve-the-name header pattern, same directory, untouched — and it is the TERMINAL state of the very card being fixed.
Two (in fact three) further instances of the identical non-wrapping header pattern inside Cards in the same module, all untouched.
data-slot was written BEFORE {...rest}, so a caller could clobber the only selector the row is addressed by.
No reactive store read in a loop/conditional, no hook-order change, no key/reconciliation change; data-*/aria-* still reach the DOM via {...rest}.

Wrapping makes the card taller at narrow widths and estimateMessageHeight was not updated, enlarging the virtualizer's first-pass estimate correction. Self-correcting via ResizeObserver; no user-visible stall.
whitespace-normal alone breaks only at spaces, so a translated label whose longest TOKEN exceeds the line is still clipped by the Card's overflow-hidden.
TEST-8 hardcoded an English-width 60px legibility floor; no `ziee-chat` string appears anywhere in the diff.
The unconditional catch converted either an environmental import failure or a real intermittent product bug into a green run.

`break-words` (overflow-wrap: break-word) does NOT break an unbroken over-long token — it is excluded from min-content sizing. Measured on a real button in this row: token gives clientWidth 236 / scrollWidth 312, height unchanged at 32px, label spilling out of the card's overflow-hidden edge. `wrap-anywhere` measures 236/236 and wraps to 50px.

The specificity note became wrong again once the rules were scoped: `& > :is(button,a)` is (0,1,1) and beats `.h-8` (0,1,0) BY specificity; only the earlier unscoped `[&>*]` form won by emission order.
The claim that the generated KIT_MANIFEST carries the child contract is false — that generator emits per-PROP rows only and this type declares no kit-authored props.
CardActions drops the `items-center` the wizard footer previously carried; with `h-auto` + default stretch, a wrapped action stretches its same-line siblings. Inert on every current call site.
CardActionsProps requires no `data-testid`, unlike sibling kit containers, so the spec must select on the `[data-slot]` implementation marker.

The tool name is still single-line `truncate` with no `title` and no expand affordance, so an attacker-chosen long name is silently ellipsised and two different tools can render identically. TEST-8 only measures a 12-char fixture, so it cannot see this.

The server label is nowrap with no truncate, so an over-long one is cut at the card's inline-end edge — strictly better than pre-fix (it can no longer displace the name or the status) but still silently truncatable.

TEST-4's presence guard asserted the length of the id list it had just mapped over, so it could never fail; a missing control then spread as `undefined` and made every geometry assertion below compare undefined to undefined and pass.

measureRow seeded its clip rect with the VIEWPORT, contradicting its own documented predicate: a control merely below the fold in the `overflow-y:auto` list would be reported as cut off by a NON-scrolling ancestor.
Both stress labels contained spaces, so they wrapped via `whitespace-normal` and never exercised the one child rule that was empirically ineffective.

TEST-5's note claimed the no-fields variant has no gallery cell; the SLUG does exist (chat/gallery.tsx:456). Re-measured: that slug renders 0 no-fields cards and 0 `elicitation-accept-no-values` buttons, so the substance (the variant is not rendered anywhere) holds, but the wording was wrong.
TEST-7 passes on both fixed and broken markup — it is a fixture precondition, not a regression test, and its title oversold it.
Two assertions restate the primitive's class list (`flexWrap === 'wrap'`, `justifyContent === 'flex-end'`) rather than a behaviour.
gotoUntilVisible's retry gate is sound in the direction that matters (a loaded-but-wrong surface rethrows on attempt 1); residual weakness is only time-to-diagnosis.

The run_js approval pair is the only remaining approve/deny outside CardActions. It uses kit `Space` (flex-wrap by default) and a non-flex title, so it carries neither broken pattern — but it orders Approve BEFORE Deny, inverting the ordering TEST-4 pins as a safety property on the MCP card.

Four of the five header wraps ship without direct test coverage (TEST-8 drives only the approval card). A tree sweep found NO other consent/approval surface still pairing a truncate primary with nowrap secondaries.
Pattern (a) is fully cleared from consent surfaces; non-consent survivors (MyMemoriesSection, ModelHubCard, ~20 Drawer footers) remain unmigrated — the scope boundary, not a consent defect.

Desktop renders the same components via `@source ../../../ui/src` and the kit path, so everything applies verbatim; the documented lg/icon re-metric hits no current call site and no committed Layer-B baselines exist to drift.
The tool name was still single-line `truncate` with no `title`: measured 238px rendered of the 534px a 64-char name needs, so an attacker-chosen name ellipsises to a benign-looking prefix.
The server label clipped 139 of its 393px at the card's overflow-hidden edge with no ellipsis and no cue, letting a hostile server conceal the tail of its own identity — the card's trust anchor.
TEST-8 was fixture-bound (12-char `get_forecast`) and could not fail for the attacker case it exists for.
The no-fields elicitation footer, changed by this branch, has zero rendered coverage; the gallery slug exists but renders 0 no-fields cards.
The JSDoc still said `break-words` after the code moved to `wrap-anywhere`.
A `gap-2` had been added to three unrelated tool-call headers; unlike flex-wrap it is not inert when content fits (8px at every width) and nothing asserted it.
TEST-3's third assertion, TEST-4, TEST-7, TEST-10b and TEST-11 pass on both fixed and broken markup by construction — legitimate guards, but not coverage of the 390px defect.
Same starvation shape outside the approval family (static app strings, so not attacker-controlled).
TEST-9's 260px squeeze is load-bearing: at 200px the virtualizer's cached row height produces a vertical clip that is an artefact of the technique.

Round 3 removed the tool name's truncation by removing its BOUND: unbounded `wrap-anywhere` hands a hostile server unlimited control of the consent card's height. Measured at 390x844 — a 6400-char name gives a 5123px card with Deny ~2800px below the fold; a 920-char name spans 1109px against an 844px viewport, so the name and the decision row cannot be on screen together. At 1280x900 the card top sits at -617. This is the exact attack the card's description clamp already exists to prevent.
The server label got the same unbounded treatment: a ~930-char label grows the card to 931px and pushes Deny to y=805 in an 844px viewport. `mcpServerParenLabel` applies no length cap.

Neither attacker-controlled string was bidi-isolated: `unicode-bidi: normal`, and an injected U+202E was preserved and reversed the visual order of everything after it, including the card's own status text.

The branch traded a disclosure defect for the ORIGINAL below-the-fold defect with nothing guarding it: TEST-10b is the suite's only vertical-fold assertion and runs at 1280x900 with the 12-char fixture name, so the mobile card-height axis was entirely unguarded.

The rewritten TEST-8 could not fail on the defect round 3 introduced: both new assertions are SATISFIED by unbounded growth (a wrapping box never has horizontal overflow; the other literally requires the box to grow). Verified true at 64/640/6400 chars while the card grew to 5123px.
The server-label half of the round-3 commit had ZERO coverage — reverting that line left all 20 tests green.
The branch's stated 'nothing this card discloses is truncated' rule was applied to one of the six headers it edited; the attacker-controlled string is still truncated on the sibling surfaces.
Desktop verified clean: it aliases straight into src-app/ui/src with no divergent copy, and the CardActions child rules measured inert at 1280px (all buttons h=32).

Round 4's clamp re-broke round 3's fix for ORDINARY names: `min-w-0 flex-1` (flex-basis:0) against a `whitespace-nowrap` status sibling never overflows its line, so the row never wrapped and the identity column got 98px of 270px at 390px (28px at 320px). `github__create_or_update_file_contents_v2` rendered 34 of 41 chars; `mcp__filesystem__read_text_file` 9 of 31 at 320px.
The server label — the card's trust anchor — was 0 of 14 characters visible by default whenever the name filled the narrow clamped column.

One click on the identity 'Show more' produced a 13343px card with Deny at y=13539 — 2.6x worse than the 5123px round 4 rated HIGH. Since ordinary names clamped, that toggle was the only way to read the name: the disclosure affordance was the exploit.

TEST-10 failed ~50% of runs on the branch as shipped (reproduced 3x, always 'span 1693px in a 844px viewport'): it wrote textContent outside React and read geometry with no wait, before the ResizeObserver-driven clamp committed. The same un-awaited pattern was in TEST-8's ceiling block.

TEST-8's disclosure assertions passed on both fixed and visually-broken code: they measured the INNER span, which a bound deliberately leaves at full intrinsic size, so they were structurally blind to what the bound hides.
The sibling elicitation and ask-user consent cards render a raw server-chosen `message` with no bound: measured 8282px and 7035px cards with Decline far below the fold, in files this branch edits.
Two CollapsibleBlocks on one consent card exposed two buttons whose accessible name was the identical string 'Show more', on the surface where identifying the tool is the whole task.
The `[unicode-bidi:isolate]` comment overstated its fix: the neighbouring status text is protected, but an RLO inside the string still reorders that string's own characters.
`approval-dest-host` is a third server-influenced string with no clamp (only `break-all`); a parsed URL host bounds the realistic case to ~180px, but nothing in code enforces the 253-char DNS limit.

The round-4 clamp DID bound the default state against every extreme input tested (6400 chars, unbroken tokens, 800 newlines, CJK, bidi, zero-width, combining marks), always ~88px region / 583px card with the full string in the DOM; its ceilings were non-vacuous under a CSS negative control.
